audience: Desktop users recovering a slow or unresponsive window, including long sessions with multiple PR tabs.
outcome: Choose Wait without interrupting work, or explicitly open local recovery; understand inactive payload eviction and saved-cache limits.
method: Agent source, factual and six-locale language delta review. Actual macOS built-main-process probes with synthetic loopback content and temporary profiles; native message-box arguments/actions automated. Prior unrelated procedural and visual evidence retained. No human reader acceptance or production-account replay claimed.
limits: Original account-specific allocation pressure and a multi-hour production session were not reproduced.
Native Windows/Linux processes were not exercised; unit coverage checks the shared controllers.
Operating-system dialog appearance was not captured; native dialog arguments and actions were verified.
Diff parsing remains synchronous; native recovery handles hangs independently of the blocked JavaScript thread.
Active data and separately saved drafts are not evicted by the inactive-payload policy; explicit native recovery can lose unsaved changes.
retainedFigures: All six applications figures remain visually applicable. The desktop-renderer-recovery page and its controls are unchanged; the new native dialog is documented by its exact labels, default choice and consequences. Original capture dates and unrelated operational evidence remain intact at article revision 8.
